page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the n2 server family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.8 GHz, with 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of memory per core. The CPU architecture is x86_64, incorporating an L1d cache of 32 KB, an L2 cache of 1.0 MB, and an L3 cache of 33 MB. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most standard operations. The server achieves an average multi-core CPU performance score of 7398.32 in stress-ng, alongside an average PassMark CPU score of 8292.45. Memory bandwidth is measured at 413.79 GB/sec for cached small blocks and approximately 50.27 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (27.31 GB/sec) and Geekbench multi-core scores (4464.0) fall into the weak category. Single-core performance is also mixed, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the weak tier at 1404.09, while Geekbench single-core scores (1170.0) remain average.

This hardware profile is suited for general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, where it demonstrates an average throughput of 6.9 GB/sec, and database operations, supported by an average Redis SET performance of 7.12 million operations per second. It is also capable of handling software compilation and basic text processing. However, the lack of local storage and GPU acceleration, combined with weak multi-threaded decompression and low LLM prompt processing speeds (340.65 tokens/sec for a 135M model), makes it less suitable for heavy data science, large-scale machine learning inference, or storage-intensive database deployments.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-8 is an x86_64 general-purpose server featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM, powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon processor with 4 physical cores and hyper-threading. The instance lacks local storage and GPU resources. Benchmark results position this server in the average tier for most operations, including a PassMark CPU score of 8292.45, a Redis SET throughput of 7.12 million operations per second, and a static web serving speed of 6.9 GB/sec. However, it exhibits weaker performance in multi-core Geekbench tests and multi-threaded decompression. This configuration is suited for balanced workloads such as web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations, but is limited for storage-heavy or compute-intensive parallel tasks due to its resource constraints and moderate multi-threaded performance.
